title: Whales and Dolphins
objective: After this level you can explain how whales and dolphins are mammals that live in the sea.
summary: Whales and dolphins breathe air through blowholes, have some hair and nurse their young. Dolphins sleep half a brain at a time. Toothed whales include dolphins; baleen whales strain food.

cards.headline: Dolphins sleep with half a brain at a time.
cards.body: Scientists think it lets them keep coming up to breathe, even while they snooze. A dolphin spends its whole life in the sea and still has to breathe air. That's your first clue that it's a mammal.

cards.headline: The checklist, passed underwater
cards.body: Whales, dolphins and porpoises meet Level 11's mammal checklist, with no discount for living at sea. They breathe air, are warm-blooded, have hair at some point in life and feed their young milk. They breathe through blowholes, nostrils on top of the head. Every breath means a trip to the surface, and the nose is already on top: a snorkel they never have to pack.

cards.fact: A dolphin calf drinks milk for about 20 months.
cards.context: A bottlenose dolphin mother is pregnant for about 12 months. Her calf nurses for about 20 months and stays with her for 3 to 6 years. That's a long childhood on milk, and about as mammal as it gets.

mascot.line: Twenty months of milk. Try telling this one it's a fish.

items.label: Baleen whales
points: No teeth: plates of keratin, like your nails
Two blowholes; they strain small prey

cards.headline: Whales and dolphins: met
learned: Warm-blooded, some hair, milk for the young

questions.prompt: How do whales and dolphins breathe?

options.label: Through gills behind the head
options.rationale: Gills belong to fish; whales have lungs.

options.label: Air through blowholes on top of the head
They take oxygen from the water

questions.explanation: Cetaceans breathe air through blowholes, nostrils on top of the head.

questions.prompt: Why do scientists think dolphins sleep with only half the brain at a time?

options.label: To dream in two ways
options.rationale: The idea is about breathing, not dreams.

options.label: So they can keep coming up to breathe
Because their brains are too small
To save heat in cold water

questions.explanation: Half-brain sleep is thought to let dolphins keep surfacing to breathe even while asleep.

questions.prompt: Level 9's blue whale lives almost entirely on krill. Which group of whales does it belong to?

options.label: Toothed whales, like dolphins
options.rationale: Toothed whales have teeth; blue whales don't.

options.label: It isn't a whale but a fish

questions.explanation: Blue whales are baleen whales: keratin plates strain krill from the water.
